step.prompt: A savings account offers 2% per year, while inflation is 5%. What happens to the real value of this money?
options: It falls by about 3% per year, even though the account balance grows
It grows by 2% per year because the bank regularly adds interest
It falls by exactly 5% per year, losing all value to inflation
It does not change because bank savings are protected
step.explanation: The real rate of return is approximately interest minus inflation (2% − 5% = −3%). Although the account balance nominally grows, the purchasing power of the money drops by about 3% per year.

step.prompt: Lena keeps €25,000 in an account with 0.5% annual interest while inflation is 3%. How much will these savings realistically be worth (in today's purchasing power) after 10 years?
step.reveal: Around €19,500. After 10 years, the nominal amount will be around €26,270, but inflation will reduce its purchasing power by more than 22%.

step.prompt: Why does compound interest generate the largest gains only after many years?
options: In subsequent years, returns are also earned on previously accumulated interest
Banks raise interest rates for long-term clients
The impact of inflation decreases to zero over time
Investments become tax-free only after 10 years
step.explanation: With compound interest, gains from previous years increase the principal and start generating returns themselves. As a result, capital growth accelerates year over year.

step.prompt: The chart shows the change in purchasing power with 0% interest and 3% inflation. After how many years will savings lose about 1/4 (25%) of their real value?
step.explanation: The chart shows that with 3% inflation, the drop in purchasing power reaches approx. −25% after 10 years ((1 / 1.03)^10 − 1 = −25.6%).

step.prompt: Assign each situation to the appropriate financial bucket:

items.text: Building retirement capital for 20 years away
3 months of expenses after job loss
Starter fund for a one-year-old child

step.explanation: An emergency fund (Notgroschen) covers sudden, unexpected expenses and must be immediately accessible. Money set aside for decades can be invested for higher returns.

step.prompt: Match the financial terms with their correct definitions:
pairs: Money for unexpected expenses, at least 3 months of living costs
Interest rate minus the inflation rate
Earning returns on capital along with previously earned interest
The duration for which money can remain invested
step.explanation: A good understanding of these 4 pillars enables safe financial planning: an emergency fund provides peace of mind, the time horizon defines strategy, compound interest builds capital, and the real rate protects against inflation.
